title: Why You Cannot Read Your Own Handwriting Sometimes
hook: You sometimes cannot read your own handwriting because your brain focuses on creation.

narration.text: You sometimes cannot read your own handwriting because your brain focuses on creation.
When you write, your brain prioritises forming letters and words quickly.
It is less concerned with perfect legibility, as it already knows what you intend.
This means your brain often takes shortcuts with letter formation.
Later, when you read, your brain tries to interpret the exact visual patterns.
But the original intent is gone, making those shortcuts look like mistakes.
It is a disconnect between the writing brain and the reading brain.
Have you ever found yourself struggling to decipher your own scribbles?

description: It is a common experience to look back at your own notes and find them impossible to read. This happens because your brain's priorities shift between writing and reading. When writing, speed and content take precedence over perfect letter formation.
